Incorporating SLOOS insights tilts the assessment more negative than the policy statement alone. Banks reported tightening standards across C&I and CRE, raising credit score thresholds and reducing credit limits, with weaker demand notably in construction and land development. They also expected further tightening for riskier loans, reduced risk tolerance, and deterioration in loan portfolios, collateral values, and HELOCs. While some banks indicated unchanged standards or demand in certain consumer categories (e.g., credit cards, some consumer loans) and some portfolios were expected to remain unchanged, the predominant signal is procyclical tightening of bank credit that can blunt transmission of the Fed’s aggressive easing and deepen near-term downside risks.

Net: negative tone, with policy backstops partially mitigating, but SLOOS implies greater credit headwinds than previously reflected.
